bending_waves: a spiral bending wave launched at a satellite's vertical resonance (epi_int_3d)¶

A self-gravitating ring of uniform surface density σ ≈ 8×10⁻⁸, 540 circular streamlines of 32 particles spanning 1 ≤ r ≤ 1.008 (ring mass 4×10⁻⁹, no viscosity), under a vertical Fourier satellite (fast/satellite.py). Its m = 2 inner vertical resonance is at r_V = 1.0064, 80% of the way across the ring. The satellite (i_s = 0.01, mass 2.5×10⁻⁷) is switched on at full mass at t = 0, and the run lasts 3500 orbits, stopping before the wave front reaches the ring's inner edge.

Each numbered section below is one test of the paper's Section 4.1 (paper equation and figure numbers as of 2026-11-13; notes/equations.md B5–B10, B13, B17–B19; Shu 1984):

  1. the wave is launched at r_V and its front moves inward at |c_g| = πGσ/ν_a (paper Eqn. 26, Fig. 4);
  2. the wave's complex amplitude h matches Shu's solution: forced response L_V/x outside r_V, and inside it a wave of constant amplitude |Z_w| (paper Eqns. 35–37);
  3. its wavenumber matches the dispersion relation, once the lattice of streamlines and the ring's edges are allowed for (paper Eqns. 25, 38, Appendix C, Fig. 5);
  4. the satellite's torque on the wave equals Shu's T_V, the wave's angular momentum luminosity, and the ring's L_z is conserved (paper Eqn. 40, Figs. 6–7);
  5. the wave leaves no mark in the ring plane;
  6. k > 0 everywhere behind the front: the wave is trailing (paper Section 4.1.1);
  7. the wave's pattern rotates prograde at the forcing's pattern speed Ω_p (paper Section 4.1.1);
  8. its first wavelength is (4πε)^{1/2} r_V (paper Section 4.1.2).

The sections after these are extras, the resolution runs and the original, narrower ring. They belong to test 9, convergence, which is on hold: their runs were not remade after the vertical-phase change (2026-11-13), so they print "not found: skipped" until test 9 resumes.

Make the output with uv run python tools/run_simulations.py tests/bending_waves (about 11 minutes). Section 7 uses a short run with dense outputs, and the extras optional runs of the original ring, made by the commands given there.

1: the wave is launched at r_V and its front moves inward at |c_g| (paper Eqn. 26, Fig. 4)¶

Each streamline's inclination, averaged over its particles, versus its fractional distance from resonance x, at six times t in units of the wave's crossing time τ_c = Δr/c_g, where Δr = r_V − 1 is the distance from resonance to the ring's inner edge and c_g = πGσ/ν is the wave's group speed (B10). The red curve is linear theory's inclination i = |h|/r, where h is Shu (1984)'s steady forced solution B8 (the paper's Eqn. 27); the particles near r_V oscillate at ω_m ≈ ν, so their inclination is |h|/r to within 0.3%. The red vertical line is the resonance, x = 0.

Switching the satellite on at full mass also starts a free vertical oscillation everywhere. At first every streamline moves as a massless particle would: through 50 orbits the simulated z follows the exact massless solution (B11, with the satellite at full mass from t = 0) to within 1.3% across the whole ring, which is why the earliest inclinations are nearly flat. Then the ring's self-gravity takes over: the response near r_V settles onto B8, and the wave it launches propagates inward behind the expected front, carrying the free disturbance at resonance with it. A small residue of that disturbance remains ahead of the front. (In the narrower ring of Section 8, growing the satellite over 160 orbits instead gave the same wave, about 160 orbits later, with a slightly smaller front overshoot and residue.)

Animations: the ring's height over the run¶

Two animations, one frame every 100 orbits, made by uv run python animate.py (about 10 s). Each plays on GitHub as a GIF, and with play, pause and a frame slider at the project's animations page:

  • bending_wave.gif: the ring seen face-on in the frame rotating with the pattern speed Ω_p, where the m = 2 spiral is stationary, with the ring's width stretched radially so the wave shows. Grayscale is the height z in units of |Z_w|, white above the plane and black below; the red dashed circle is r_V. Each streamline's particles are interpolated along the streamline with a periodic spline in longitude.
  • bending_wave_lines.gif: every 3rd streamline's particles joined by a line, z versus longitude in the same frame, each offset by its distance from resonance x. |Z_w| is drawn as two curve spacings, so curves overlap where neighbours are out of phase, and the crests show as dark bands.

2: the wave's complex amplitude h against Shu's solution (paper Eqns. 35–37)¶

Each streamline's h is a least-squares fit of its particles' z = Re(h) cos χ − Im(h) sin χ, where χ = mθ − (m+1)λ_s + Ω_s is the forcing's phase. The red curve is Shu's steady solution (paper Eqn. 35, B8); dotted lines mark the front expected from the group velocity, x_f = −|c_g|t/r_V. Behind the front the wave part h − L_V/x should have the constant amplitude |Z_w| (paper Eqn. 37), and outside the resonance zone h should be the forced response.

3: the wavenumber against the dispersion relation (paper Eqns. 25, 38, Appendix C, Fig. 5)¶

The local wavenumber is the radial derivative of the phase of the wave part h − L_V/x, from the simulation and from B8. It is compared with three dispersion relations (wave_wavenumber, B13): the continuum's 𝒟|x| = 2πGσk (B7, which B8 also assumes), the lattice of streamlines spaced Δ, 𝒟|x| = X(kΔ), and that lattice cut off at the ring's edges, 𝒟|x| = X(kΔ) − 2Gσ(1/d_in + 1/d_out), since the ring lacks the pull of the streamlines beyond its edges.

In [5]:

fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 8), sharex=True)
axs[0].plot(xm, k_sim, 'k.', ms=3, label='simulation')
axs[0].plot(xm, k_B8, 'r-', lw=0.8, label='B8')

plt.tight_layout()
for name, kk in (('continuum', k_cont), ('lattice', k_lat), ('lattice + edges', k_edge)):

4: the satellite's torque is the wave's angular momentum luminosity; L_z is conserved (paper Eqn. 40, Figs. 6–7)¶

The torque that the satellite's resonant potential A_V z sin χ exerts on the simulated ring, −Σ μ m A_V z cos χ summed over particles (B9's integrand), accumulated inward from the outer edge, against the same sum over B8's h; and the ring's total over time, against B9, T = −π²mσr_V²A_V²/𝒟. fast/satellite.py applies only the satellite's vertical pull, so the ring's own angular momentum does not change.

Shu's torque T_V (paper Eqn. 40, B9) is also the angular momentum luminosity of the wave the satellite launches. Below it, the ring's own L_z over time (paper Fig. 7), which only the ring's gravity and round-off can change.

In [6]:
T_B9 = -np.pi**2*sat.m*sigma*sat.r_V**2*A_V**2/D
T = satellite_torque(p, o, -1)

T_B8 = -sat.m*A_V*mu_s*hB8.real/2

axs[0].set_xlabel(r'$x$'); axs[0].set_ylabel(r'torque outside $x$, $/|T_{B9}|$'); axs[0].legend(fontsize=10)
axs[0].xaxis.set_major_locator(plt.MaxNLocator(5))

      f'mean over the last half of the run: {Tt[len(Tt)//2:].mean()/T_B9:.3f}')

5: no in-plane motion¶

The satellite pulls only vertically, and the ring's in-plane self-gravity is weak, so the streamlines should stay circular and in place.

Each streamline's eccentricity e at the same times, averaged over its particles. The satellite pulls only vertically, so the wave should leave no mark in the plane, and none shows. The steady V shape is not orbital motion: the elements (V3) are computed with the planet's gravity alone, while each streamline circles in the planet's and the ring's gravity. The ring's radial pull, zero mid-ring and largest at the edges, makes a circular orbit's speed differ from the planet-only circular speed by δv/v ≈ g_ring r/(2v²), read as e ≈ 2δv/v ≈ 10⁻⁶ at the edges. The particles actually move radially by only ~4×10⁻⁸ (Section 6), and e changes over the run by far less than its V shape (printed).

In [8]:

6: k > 0 behind the front: the wave is trailing (paper Section 4.1.1)¶

The dispersion relation fixes only |k|. The wave carries its angular momentum away from the resonance, inward at an inner vertical resonance, which requires k > 0, a trailing wave (paper Section 4.1.1). Below, each particle's z at the end, against x and longitude θ: the two arms wind tighter inward and trail, their longitude decreasing outward. Then the sign of the simulated wavenumber of test 3, behind the front.

In [10]:

ax.axvline(0, color='k', lw=0.5, ls=':')
ax.set_xlabel(r'$x = (r - r_V)/r_V$'); ax.set_ylabel(r'longitude $\theta$')
fig.colorbar(s, label=r'$z/|Z_w|$')
ax.set_title(f'{orbits[-1]:.0f} orbits')
plt.tight_layout()
k_beh = k_sim[sel]
print(f'behind the front: {np.sum(k_beh > 0)} of {k_beh.size} wavenumbers are positive (trailing); '
      f'smallest k/k_continuum = {np.min(k_beh/k_cont):.3f}')

7: the pattern rotates prograde at Ω_p (paper Section 4.1.1)¶

A wave Re[h e^{i(mθ − ωt)}] rotates at the pattern speed Ω_p = ω/m (paper Section 4.1.1): in the inertial frame each streamline's amplitude g, from a fit of z = Re[g e^{imθ}], has arg g decreasing at the rate mΩ_p. The main run's outputs are 50 orbits apart, while the phase advances by about 6 radians per orbit, so on their own they cannot tell Ω_p from its aliases Ω_p + 2πn/(mΔt), spaced 0.01 apart, nor even its sign. So it is measured in two steps:

  1. A short run of the same ring, 250 orbits with an output every 1.5 time units and 8 particles per streamline, made from this folder by

    uv run python ../../fast/epi_int_3d.py -m '{"particles_per_streamline": 8, "number_of_particles": 4320, "timesteps_per_output": 3, "total_number_of_outputs": 1047, "output_folder": "output_pattern"}'

    (under a minute), gives Ω_p from a linear fit of the unwrapped arg g against time (T14) over its last 150 orbits. That early in the run the wave has barely left r_V, and each streamline also carries the free oscillation that switching the satellite on started, at a different pattern speed, so the fit is good only near r_V, to about 10⁻³. That is enough to pick the alias.

  2. The main run, behind the front late in the run, where the wave is established, refines it: the same fit of arg g + mΩ_dense t over the outputs after 0.65 τ_c.

Both are compared with the forcing's Ω_p = Ω_{a_s} + ν_{a_s}/m.

In [11]:
Om_p = sat.Omega_p
#step 1: the dense run, near r_V
pp, op = load3d('.', modified_params={'particles_per_streamline': 8, 'number_of_particles': 4320,
                                      'timesteps_per_output': 3, 'total_number_of_outputs': 1047,
                                      'output_folder': 'output_pattern'})
ks_d = np.where(op['times'] > 100*2*np.pi)[0]
xp = (op['r'][0].mean(axis=1) - sat.r_V)/sat.r_V
near = np.where(np.abs(xp) < np.sqrt(eps))[0]
Om_dense = np.median([pattern_speed(pp, op, j, ks_d, sat.m)[0] for j in near])
print(f'step 1, dense run, {len(near)} streamlines within eps^1/2 of r_V: Omega_p = {Om_dense:.6f}, '
      f'/forcing - 1 = {Om_dense/Om_p - 1:+.1e}; alias spacing 2 pi/(m dt) = {2*np.pi/(sat.m*np.diff(o["times"])[0]):.4f}')
#step 2: the main run, behind the front, late
ks_m = np.where(o['times'] > 0.65*tau_c)[0]
js = np.where(behind)[0]
fit = np.array([pattern_speed(p, o, j, ks_m, sat.m, guess=Om_dense) for j in js])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.5))
ax.plot(x[js], fit[:, 0]/Om_p - 1, 'k.', ms=4)
ax.axhline(0, color='b', lw=0.5)
ax.set_xlabel(r'$x = (r - r_V)/r_V$'); ax.set_ylabel(r'$\Omega_{p,\rm fit}/\Omega_p - 1$')
ax.set_title(f'behind the front, {len(ks_m)} outputs after 0.65 $\\tau_c$')
plt.tight_layout()
print(f'step 2, main run, {len(js)} streamlines behind the front: Omega_p median {np.median(fit[:, 0]):.7f}, forcing {Om_p:.7f}, '
      f'median /forcing - 1 = {np.median(fit[:, 0])/Om_p - 1:+.1e}, largest |.| = {np.abs(fit[:, 0]/Om_p - 1).max():.1e}, '
      f'largest rms phase residual {fit[:, 1].max():.3f} rad; all positive (prograde): {np.all(fit[:, 0] > 0)}')

8: the first wavelength is (4πε)^{1/2} r_V (paper Section 4.1.2)¶

Shu's wave has phase −x²/2ε (paper Eqn. 36c), so its first wavelength, from r_V to where that phase reaches 2π, is (4πε)^{1/2} r_V (paper Section 4.1.2, B18). Fit the unwrapped phase of the simulated wave part h − L_V/x behind the front to φ₀ + c x², giving ε_fit = −1/(2c), and compare the first wavelength it implies with theory's. This is test 3's wavenumber integrated once, k = −x/(ε r_V), so the lattice and edges lengthen k, and shorten the wavelength, here too.

In [12]:
eps_fit, rms = quadratic_phase(x[behind], (h - f_V)[behind])
eps_B8, _ = quadratic_phase(x[behind], (hB8 - f_V)[behind])
lam1 = lambda e: np.sqrt(4*np.pi*e)*sat.r_V
print(f'eps = {eps:.4g}; from the phase of the simulated wave {eps_fit:.4g} (rms residual {rms:.2f} rad), of Shu\'s {eps_B8:.4g}')
print(f'first wavelength (4 pi eps)^1/2 r_V: theory {lam1(eps):.4g}, simulation {lam1(eps_fit):.4g} '
      f'(ratio {lam1(eps_fit)/lam1(eps):.3f}), = {lam1(eps)/(p["radial_width"]/(p["number_of_streamlines"] - 1)):.0f} streamline spacings')

Extra: resolution (test 9, on hold: not rerun)¶

On the original ring of the next section (half as wide, a quarter as massive, 270 streamlines), which is four times cheaper to run: that run, and the same with twice the particles per streamline or twice the streamlines, made from this folder by

uv run python ../../fast/epi_int_3d.py -m '{"radial_width": 0.004, "total_ring_mass": 1.0e-9, "number_of_streamlines": 270, "number_of_particles": 8640, "satellite": {"resonance": "vertical", "m": 2, "mass_final": 2.5e-7, "time_grow": -1.0, "r": 2.090314689118, "t": 0.0, "inclination": 0.01, "node": 0.0}, "output_folder": "output_narrow"}'

and the same with "particles_per_streamline": 64, "number_of_particles": 17280, "output_folder": "output_narrow_np64" or "number_of_streamlines": 540, "number_of_particles": 17280, "output_folder": "output_narrow_ns540" (about 3, 6 and 12 minutes). With twice the particles per streamline nothing should change. With twice the streamlines, the lattice's part of the wavenumber excess should halve, while the edges' part stays.

In [13]:
import satellite as satellite_module
narrow = {'radial_width': 0.004, 'total_ring_mass': 1.0e-9, 'number_of_streamlines': 270, 'number_of_particles': 8640,
          'satellite': dict(p['satellite'], r=2.090314689118), 'output_folder': 'output_narrow'}

def run_stats(pv, ov):
    # the comparisons of tests 2-4 for another run: wavenumber against the three dispersion relations, amplitude
    # and torque, behind the front at the end of the run
    sv = satellite_module.Satellite(pv['satellite'], pv['J2'], pv['Rp'])
    sg = ring_sigma(pv)
    A = sv.mass_final*sv.A_V_per_mass
    Zw = A*np.sqrt(sv.r_V/(sg*sv.D_V))
    xi = (1 - sv.r_V)/sv.r_V
    _, xv, hv = simulated_h(pv, ov, -1)
    fv = 1j*A/(sv.D_V*xv)
    xmv = 0.5*(xv[1:] + xv[:-1])
    kv = np.angle((hv - fv)[1:]/(hv - fv)[:-1])/np.diff(xv)/sv.r_V
    s = (xmv < 0.125*xi) & (xmv > 0.56*xi)
    kc, kl, ke = wave_wavenumber(pv, sv, xmv[s])
    b = (xv < 0.125*xi) & (xv > 0.56*xi)
    T_B9v = -np.pi**2*sv.m*sg*sv.r_V**2*A**2/sv.D_V
    Tv = np.array([satellite_torque(pv, ov, k).sum() for k in range(len(ov['times']))])/T_B9v
    late = ov['times'] > 600*2*np.pi
    return (f'median k/k - 1: continuum {np.median(kv[s]/kc - 1):+.3f}, lattice {np.median(kv[s]/kl - 1):+.3f}, '
            f'lattice + edges {np.median(kv[s]/ke - 1):+.3f};  median |wave|/|Z_w| {np.median(np.abs(hv - fv)[b])/Zw:.3f};  '
            f'torque/B9 {Tv[late].mean():.3f}')

print(f'{"this ring":19s} {p["number_of_streamlines"]} x {p["particles_per_streamline"]}: {run_stats(p, o)}')
for folder, extra in (('output_narrow', {}),
                      ('output_narrow_np64', {'particles_per_streamline': 64, 'number_of_particles': 17280}),
                      ('output_narrow_ns540', {'number_of_streamlines': 540, 'number_of_particles': 17280})):
    if not Path(folder).exists():
        print(folder, 'not found: skipped')
        continue
    pv, ov = load3d('.', modified_params=dict(narrow, output_folder=folder, **extra))
    print(f'{folder:19s} {pv["number_of_streamlines"]} x {pv["particles_per_streamline"]}: {run_stats(pv, ov)}')

Extra: the original ring, half as wide (test 9, on hold: not rerun)¶

The test as first run: 270 streamlines spanning 1 ≤ r ≤ 1.004, mass 10⁻⁹, so σ is half this ring's, and the satellite at a_s = 2.09031 puts r_V = 1.0032 at 80% of the way across. With half the σ, the wavelength at a given x and the group speed are halved, so the crossing time τ_c and the resolution at the inner edge (11 streamlines per wavelength) are the same as here, but the ring holds half as many crests and its outer edge is only 2.8 resonance-zone widths from r_V. It is output_narrow of the resolution section.

In [14]:
if not Path('output_narrow').exists():
    print('output_narrow not found: skipped')
else:
    import satellite as satellite_module
    pw, ow = load3d('.', modified_params=narrow)
    satw = satellite_module.Satellite(pw['satellite'], pw['J2'], pw['Rp'])
    sigw = ring_sigma(pw)
    A_Vw = satw.mass_final*satw.A_V_per_mass
    Z_ww = A_Vw*np.sqrt(satw.r_V/(sigw*satw.D_V))
    c_gw = np.pi*sigw/nu_a(pw['J2'], pw['Rp'], satw.r_V)
    tau_cw = (satw.r_V - 1.0)/c_gw
    _, xw, hw = simulated_h(pw, ow, -1)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5.5))
    xs = np.linspace(xw.min(), xw.max(), 40000)
    ax.plot(xs, np.abs(bending_wave(satw, sigw, xs))/(satw.r_V*(1 + xs))/1e-6, 'r-', lw=1.5, label='linear theory, B8')
    for frac, c in zip(picks, plt.cm.viridis(np.linspace(0, 0.9, len(picks)))):
        k = np.argmin(np.abs(ow['times'] - frac*tau_cw))
        xk = ((ow['a'][k] - satw.r_V)/satw.r_V).mean(axis=1)
        ax.plot(xk, ow['inc'][k].mean(axis=1)/1e-6, '.-', ms=2, lw=0.6, color=c,
                label=rf'$t = {ow["times"][k]/tau_cw:.2f}\,\tau_c$')
    ax.axvline(0, color='r', lw=1)
    ax.set_xlim(xw.min(), xw.max()); ax.set_ylim(0, 1.6*Z_ww/satw.r_V/1e-6)
    ax.set_xlabel(r'$x = (r - r_V)/r_V$'); ax.set_ylabel(r'inclination $i$ ($10^{-6}$ rad)')
